The subtraction B_m E_m-B_(m-1)E_(m-1)=k^m T^m(z) proves convergence of averages iff ordinary orbit converges. The tent fixed points 0,2/3 have expanding derivatives of magnitude 2, so convergent orbits eventually land on these points; only countably many preimages do. For typical dense orbits, every backward tent history arises as a subsequential endpoint configuration. The inverse-branch inequality w_-j+w_-(j-1)/2<=1 gives upper weighted average 2k/(2k+1); zero history attains 0 and repeated right inverse beginning at w0=1 attains the upper bound. Monotone plateau averaging and |A_(N+1)-A_N|<=1/(N+1) fill all intermediate limits. Independently checked exact fractional plateau telescoping and extremizing backwards history for k=2..7, length 80. These are corroborative; ergodic density and compactness prove the infinite assertion.
